name: BioGRID ORCS (Open Repository of CRISPR Screens)
scope: Curated CRISPR screen results from 418 publications (home page); human screens bundled in BIOGRID-ORCS-ALL-homo_sapiens-LATEST.screens.tar.gz.

quantitative.summary: Per-screen scores and hit calls, protocol-dependent.

licence.name: MIT License (stated on the BioGRID download repository page for BioGRID-ORCS; data provided without warranty)
licence.redistribution: Free for academic and commercial use under the MIT License; cite the original contributing authors and Stark et al. 2006 (Nucleic Acids Res 34:D535). This repository does not redistribute the archive.

coverage_limitations: Screen design, cell line and readout vary widely; hits are not directly comparable
known_omissions: Variant-level perturbation (base editing) screens are not its focus

reuse_decision.rationale: Open Targets lists evidence_crispr/evidence_crispr_screen, but its source mix is not verified to equal ORCS; fetch the human bundle for gene-level screen detail.

mechanism_evidence.note: whole-gene perturbation in the screened system; not allele-specific

evidence_profile.biological_context: Curated results of CRISPR screens in cell lines and cell types of several model organisms. Every hit is conditional on the screen's cell line, library, perturbation type and phenotype readout.
evidence_profile.evidence_strength: Curated from publications. Hit calls and scores follow each study's own method and threshold and are not uniformly reprocessed.
evidence_profile.mechanistic_confidence: Moderate for the effect of perturbing the whole gene in the tested context. No particular allele is described, and compensation by paralogs or pathways is not resolved.
evidence_profile.phenotype_implication: Gene-level cellular phenotype in vitro (for example viability or drug response); not an organismal or human phenotype.
evidence_profile.absence_means: A gene that is not a hit was not scored as a hit in the curated screens; power, context and threshold limit this. It is not shown to be dispensable elsewhere, and its alleles are not shown to be tolerated.

overlaps_with_sources.note: both report cancer cell-line perturbation screens; keep both and compare, do not count a gene twice when the same screen appears in both
